stem: An analyst team wants one reusable product filtering query that takes a category supplied at run time. A reviewer objects to assembling the statement by pasting the supplied text into the string, and asks for the safe construction instead.

option_texts.A: Use a parameter marker, which separates provided values from the structure of the statement
option_texts.B: Build the statement with string concatenation but escape every quote in the supplied text
option_texts.C: Wrap the statement in a view, because a view cannot be subverted by a supplied value
option_texts.D: Validate the supplied text against a list of categories before pasting it into the string

drill_answer_short: Parameter markers protect against SQL injection by separating provided values from statement structure
decision_hinge: Using parameter markers protects your code from SQL injection attacks since it clearly separates provided values from the structure of the SQL statements.

plausible_options.D: A reviewer objects to assembling the statement by pasting the supplied text into the string

eliminated_by.B: asks for the safe construction instead
eliminated_by.C: one reusable product filtering query that takes a category supplied at run time

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - escaping by hand is the fragile practice the reviewer is objecting to
distractor_traps.C: T2: scope error - a view fixes the query text and cannot accept a run time value
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - an allow list narrows the risk but still builds the statement by pasting

stem: A statement already carries one marker referenced by name, and an engineer adds a second value positionally to save typing. The statement now fails to run, and the team wants the rule that explains it.

option_texts.A: Markers are allowed only once per statement, so the second one is rejected
option_texts.B: Markers referenced by name and markers referenced by position cannot be mixed in one statement
option_texts.C: Markers cannot be referenced from a WHERE clause, which is where the second sits
option_texts.D: Markers must be declared in the order they appear, and the second broke the order

drill_answer_short: You cannot mix named and unnamed parameter markers in the same SQL statement
decision_hinge: You cannot mix named and unnamed parameter markers in the same SQL statement.

plausible_options.D: an engineer adds a second value positionally to save typing

eliminated_by.A: A statement already carries one marker referenced by name
eliminated_by.C: the team wants the rule that explains it

distractor_traps.A: T1: fabricated - a statement may carry many markers of one kind
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - a marker is perfectly legal in a WHERE clause
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - ordering matters for unnamed markers, but the failure is the mixing

stem: A bronze table keeps a payload column as a STRING holding a JSON document, and the silver model needs its fields addressable as real columns. The team already knows the shape the document takes.

option_texts.A: Cast the column to a struct type, which reads the document and types its fields
option_texts.B: Apply to_json to the column, which converts the text into addressable fields
option_texts.C: Apply from_json with the known schema, which returns a struct value to address
option_texts.D: Apply explode to the column, which turns each document key into its own row

drill_answer_short: from_json(jsonStr, schema) returns a struct value whose fields can then be selected
decision_hinge: The from_json function returns a struct value with the given jsonStr and schema.

plausible_options.A: the silver model needs its fields addressable as real columns

eliminated_by.B: keeps a payload column as a STRING holding a JSON document
eliminated_by.D: The team already knows the shape the document takes

distractor_traps.A: T5: common misconception - a plain cast does not parse a JSON document into a struct
distractor_traps.B: T3: confusable sibling - to_json runs the other way, rendering a value as JSON text
distractor_traps.D: T2: scope error - explode expands an array into rows, it does not parse a document

stem: A pipeline declares an incrementally loaded object and the team wants one statement that both defines it and brings it up to date on later runs. They would rather not pair a create with a separate refresh step.

option_texts.A: CREATE STREAMING TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, paired with a refresh command on later runs
option_texts.B: CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW, which is the only object that refreshes from a declaration
option_texts.C: CREATE OR REPLACE STREAMING TABLE, which defines the object afresh on every run
option_texts.D: CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE, which both defines the object and refreshes it

drill_answer_short: CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE defines the streaming table and refreshes it on subsequent runs
decision_hinge: The statement form is CREATE OR REFRESH STREAMING TABLE or CREATE STREAMING TABLE IF NOT EXISTS followed by the table name and table specification.

plausible_options.A: the team wants one statement that both defines it and brings it up to date on later runs

eliminated_by.B: They would rather not pair a create with a separate refresh step
eliminated_by.C: A pipeline declares an incrementally loaded object

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - that form does exist, but it needs the separate refresh the team is avoiding
distractor_traps.B: T2: scope error - a materialized view recomputes rather than loading incrementally
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - rebuilding from scratch is not what the streaming form does

stem: A bundle has been deployed and declares a job under the resource key sales_job. The engineer wants to start exactly that job in the target workspace from the command line, without clicking through the jobs list.

option_texts.A: A bundle run naming the key, which runs the job declared under that key
option_texts.B: A bundle deploy naming the key, since deploying a single resource also starts it
option_texts.C: A bundle validate naming the key, which executes the resource it checks
option_texts.D: A jobs submit call naming the key, since the CLI resolves keys to job ids

drill_answer_short: databricks bundle run [KEY] runs the job, pipeline or app declared under that key
decision_hinge: The bundle run command runs a job, pipeline, app, or script, and you specify the job, pipeline, or app key declared within the bundle configuration files.

plausible_options.D: wants to start exactly that job in the target workspace from the command line

eliminated_by.B: A bundle has been deployed and declares a job under the resource key sales_job
eliminated_by.C: without clicking through the jobs list

distractor_traps.B: T5: common misconception - deploying publishes the definition and does not trigger a run
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - validate checks configuration and never executes a resource
distractor_traps.D: T3: confusable sibling - a jobs API call needs the job id, not the bundle resource key

stem: A team is writing its contribution guide and has to state which steps happen inside the workspace folder and which belong to the hosting provider. Reviewers must know where to go once a feature branch has been pushed.

option_texts.A: Branch creation happens in the provider, while review and merge happen in the folder
option_texts.B: Branch creation happens in the folder, while the review and merge happen in the provider
option_texts.C: Both branch creation and review happen in the folder, which mirrors them upstream
option_texts.D: Both branch creation and review happen in the provider, with the folder read-only

drill_answer_short: Branches are created and pushed from the Git folder, but pull requests are raised in the Git provider's interface
decision_hinge: You create a branch and commit and push from the Git folder, and you use your Git provider's interface to create a pull request and merge it into the default branch.

plausible_options.A: which steps happen inside the workspace folder and which belong to the hosting provider

eliminated_by.C: Reviewers must know where to go once a feature branch has been pushed
eliminated_by.D: A team is writing its contribution guide

distractor_traps.A: T3: confusable sibling - the two halves are the right pair but swapped round
distractor_traps.C: T1: fabricated - no review surface exists inside the workspace folder
distractor_traps.D: T5: common misconception - the folder is fully writable and is where branches are cut
